speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) with pseudovirilism and delayed menarche.

This patient presents with classic signs of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, including virilization (clitoromegaly, labial fusion) and signs of androgen excess (severe acne, maternal hirsutism during pregnancy), alongside delayed menarche. The history of fractures on minor trauma could be due to underlying osteoporosis from chronic steroid exposure or a concurrent condition, but the primary syndrome is clearly CAH. I will request hormone levels to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone, Testosterone, DHEA-S, and ACTH stimulation test.
